questions.q: What keyword must every IF calculation in Tableau end with?
questions.explain: Every IF block in Tableau must be closed with END, or the Calculation Editor shows a syntax error and refuses to save.

questions.q: In IF [Profit] > 0 THEN "Profitable" ELSEIF [Profit] = 0 THEN "Break Even" ELSE "Loss" END, what does a row with Profit exactly equal to 0 return?
questions.explain: The first condition (Profit > 0) is false for exactly 0, so Tableau checks the ELSEIF — Profit = 0 — which matches and returns "Break Even".

questions.q: What happens to a row that matches none of the conditions in an IF statement if you omit the ELSE clause?
options: It causes a syntax error and the calculation won't save
It automatically returns the first THEN value
questions.explain: ELSE is technically optional, but without it, any row matching none of the conditions returns NULL — which is rarely what you actually want.

questions.q: Which situation is CASE better suited for than IF?
options: Testing the same field against a short list of exact values, like matching [Region] to "East", "West", and "Central"
Combining two different fields with AND
Any calculation that doesn't require an ELSE
questions.explain: CASE is built for testing one field against a list of specific known values — cleaner than IF/ELSEIF for that shape of problem, while IF is better for ranges, comparisons, and multiple fields.

questions.q: In CASE [Region] WHEN "East" THEN "E" WHEN "West" THEN "W" ELSE "?" END, what does a row with Region = "South" return?
options: "?" — because South doesn't match either WHEN clause, so ELSE catches it
NULL — because CASE has no ELSE support
A syntax error, since South wasn't explicitly handled
questions.explain: Since "South" doesn't match "East" or "West", the ELSE branch catches it and returns "?", exactly like ELSE does in an IF statement.
